title: openKRX --json envelope, schema_version 1
description: The single JSON object openkrx writes on stdout in --json mode. It describes what the executable in this repository emits and is not a statement about any external format, profile or service: `verified` is always false, because openKRX performs no cryptography, and `ok` is about the command rather than about the package. Adding a field to the envelope does not raise `schema_version`, so a consumer must ignore fields it does not recognise; every object a command's report is built from therefore leaves `additionalProperties` open. The two closed objects are `diagnostic` and `cleanup`: a diagnostic may carry only a stable code, its category, an entry index, a manifest pointer and counts, never a path, an entry name or a value an author wrote, and closing them makes that privacy rule checkable rather than merely documented. The commands `skill`, `completions` and `man` bypass the envelope and are described by nothing here.

schema_version.description: The envelope version. A consumer that reads a version it does not know must stop rather than guess.

ok.description: Whether stdout carries a report rather than a diagnostic. It says nothing about the package: a failed structural check is part of a successful command's report. Read `data.summary` or the exit status to decide about a package.

verified.description: Always false. openKRX performs no cryptography, so no run of it can report that anything was verified.

command.description: The stable name of the command that produced the envelope. `skill`, `completions` and `man` never appear: they write their bytes outside the envelope.

code.description: A stable dotted code, catalogued in docs/codes.md. The head is one of the eight `scripts/check-codes.py` extracts; the remaining segments are lower-case letters, digits and underscores. An unrecognised code is a failure, never a success.

category.description: The coarse family the code belongs to. It is the same category that decided the process exit status, so a consumer that groups rather than branches can read either. `success` is not among them: a diagnostic is never a success.

rule.description: A rule of docs/profile.md that no primary source settles, such as `A19` or `M13`.

hex.description: Lower-case hexadecimal of raw bytes, reported when the bytes are not valid UTF-8 and no faithful string form exists.

count.description: A measured non-negative count of bytes, entries or files.

diagnostic.description: The single content-free diagnostic of a failed run. Closed on purpose: no field beyond these may appear, because a diagnostic may never carry an input path, an entry name or a value an author wrote. Every field but `code` and `category` is present only when the refusal carries it.

entry_index.description: The archive entry the refusal is about, counted in central-directory order.

field.description: A JSON Pointer into the manifest, or into the edits document, naming a location the caller wrote and never a value from it. `create` and `repack` only.

attachment_index.description: Position in the manifest's or the edits document's attachment array, counted from 0. `create` and `repack` only.

attachment_number.description: An attachment's number inside the package being edited, counted from 1, which is a different thing from a position in an array. `repack` alone sets it.

limit.description: The ceiling that was exceeded, for a limit refusal.

observed.description: What was actually produced against that ceiling: a measured count of bytes or entries, never a size a header declared.

cleanup.description: What the undo pass removed, present on a failed run of the three commands that write. Counts, never a path; closed for the same privacy reason as `diagnostic`. `left_in_place` above 0 means the destination is not as it was found.

outcome.description: What one check concluded, without naming the check. `code` is present only on a failure and `rule` only when a rule of docs/profile.md is undecided; an undecided rule is never shown as a pass and never as a failure.

check.description: One named structural check and what it concluded, in the documented order of the check inventory.

unresolvedRules.description: Each rule the checks left undecided, once, in the order they first cite it.

layout.description: The one layout openKRX writes. It is documented and unverified against any real producer, and naming it is not a conformance claim.

capabilitiesData.description: `capabilities`: machine-readable implementation status, never a verification verdict.

operations.description: The package operations a command actually performs. `skill`, `completions` and `man` are not package operations and never appear.

inspectData.description: `inspect`: what the package declares about itself, and every check. Nothing here is interpreted.

metadata.description: The declared document when one was located and parsed, and null otherwise.

observations.description: Facts about the archive's shape, independent of the document. A `_hex` field is present only when the corresponding bytes are not valid UTF-8, and then the text field is absent.

metadata.description: The declared fields of a parsed document, exactly as it wrote them. `created_at` keeps its lexical form because the crate has no clock.

test_present.description: Whether the element was actually present; its absence is rule M11.

attachment.description: One declared attachment reference and the entry it resolved to. The declared size keeps its verbatim text because rule M13 leaves its unit and rounding open; a declared and an observed size are reported side by side and never compared.

declared_size_value.description: The declared size read as a number, present only when it reads as a finite one.

listData.description: `list`: every archive entry, in central-directory order. Profile-agnostic: it says what the ZIP image contains and nothing about KRX.

entry.description: One archive entry as the inventory observed it. `name` is present when the name bytes are valid UTF-8 and `name_hex` only when they are not; a declared size and the size the decoder produced are reported side by side.

name_utf8_flag.description: General-purpose bit 11, reported independently of whether the bytes decode.

crc32.description: The declared CRC-32 as eight lower-case hexadecimal digits. A CRC detects corruption and says nothing about authenticity.

validateStructureData.description: `validate-structure`: the check inventory, outcome by outcome. The summary word says only whether anything failed and whether anything was left open; it is never a verdict on a package.

extractData.description: `extract`: the record of what was written, built as each file was created. Paths are relative to the destination and joined with `/` on every platform; the destination itself is never reported.

directories_created.description: Directories this run created. One that already existed is not counted.

marker_removed.description: Whether the partial marker was removed, which ends a complete run.

path_resolution_fallback.description: Whether this run asked the kernel to resolve every path beneath one directory descriptor, could not have it, and used the portable check-then-create path instead. False where there was no stronger mode to ask for.

written.description: One file that exists on disk because this run created it.

createData.description: `create`: what was written, and what reading it straight back reported. `unresolved_rules` comes from openKRX reading the package back with its own structural check before the command reported anything.

repackData.description: `repack`: what changed, what did not, and what reading the result said. The four attachment lists carry numbers, never names: `preserved`, `changed` and `removed` by their number in the package that was read, `added` by the number the new attachment took in the package that was written.

header_fields.description: The header fields the edits set, by their manifest spelling. Field names only: no value an edits document carried is reported.
